findings.reason: as written the done-when is unmeetable (read_blobs keeps its own subprocess call), so the runner interface must name stdin/payload support or the done-when must be re-scoped to the callers that fit it.
findings.text: §13 extends `service._run` with "a byte mode and the one 180-second timeout" and its done-when asserts `grep -rn 'subprocess' reckon/velocity.py` reports ONE invoking function, but velocity.py carries four subprocess sites today and `read_blobs` (:373) feeds git on stdin (`input=payload`), a capability the described interface does not carry

findings.reason: the mechanical reuse is right but the owner is wrong-domain and inverts layering, so the runner belongs in a neutral low-level module (or the plan must justify the core→crew dependency), otherwise future git callers extend an owner whose docstring scopes it to serving the HTTP daemon.
findings.text: extending `service._run` into the package-wide process owner makes core `reckon/velocity.py` import `reckon.service`, whose top-level `from reckon.crew.paid_lanes import systemd_user_dir` (service.py:20) drags in the crew layer; verified: `import reckon.velocity` currently pulls no crew module, and would after this change

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §13's runner interface cannot absorb `read_blobs`, the git caller its own done-when requires it to hide.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the runner §13 extends is homed in `reckon/service.py`, the systemd-user-unit manager, so the core layer would import the crew layer.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §12 states net zero (adds the velocity sources reader, retires the public `revised_python`) and §13 states net one (adds the process runner and `cache_root`, retires `pick_input_cache_root`), and neither section adds a CLI option, MCP view or refusal family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the codebase it extends and cites what it found: `read_blobs` (velocity.py:360), `_plan_documents` (velocity.py:306), `read_trees` (interface_counts.py:441), `service._run` (service.py:206) and the five cache cascades; its counts (1,169 tracked `.py` at HEAD, 98 outside `reckon/` and `tests/`) reproduce exactly, and no other `ls-tree -r` lister or archive-based source reader exists to miss.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `read_trees` becomes parse-over-the-shared-reader rather than a parallel reader, and the retention of `routing._git` is justified in-plan as error-domain translation that delegates to the runner; the new public sources reader is the consolidation itself, not a wrapper over an extendable owner.
